risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Ordinary authoring and object changes follow registered data execution with verified cached authority. Risk tier does not impose RealmCommit age, online origin or periodic freshness on ordinary publication.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Registered high-risk approvals and explicit validity constraints are enforced. Security writes revalidate exact authority and preconditions in the unique confirmation sequence; risk labels do not override execution classification.

eligibility_kind_definitions.event_submission_carrier: The action executes through a durable Event. An approval requirement is expressible because the registered Event submission operation carries approval evidence beside the complete Event.
eligibility_kind_definitions.registered_operation_carrier: The non-Event action names an explicit operation carrier override whose canonical closed request schema contains the registered evidence field.
eligibility_kind_definitions.ineligible_no_registered_carrier: The action has no registered evidence carrier. A grant approval constraint and an ak.policy.action approval requirement targeting this action are forbidden in v1.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant, except for a root_control_only or subject_only action, whose authority is the registered root-control or subject binding, and except for the subject-bound branches the owning section registers for that event kind (the invitee decline and the joined inviter self-cancel of ak.invite.cancel, zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3).

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root typed current result may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

approval_requirement_eligibility is the only v1 decision source for whether a grant approval constraint or ak.policy.action approval requirement may target an action. Every event_mapping_kind resolves through event_mapping_defaults; a non_event_surface action is ineligible unless one exact action_overrides row selects registered_operation_carrier and names a reachable carrier. Implementations MUST NOT infer eligibility from action spelling, risk tier, prose, or an invented action-to-operation mapping.

actions.notes: Authorizes a service-actor signed bridge error Event only for the exact active Applet installation, registration epoch and granted scope. The Event still carries applet_id and a real authorization_ref; service signature is provenance, not authority.

Authorizes only actor_role=ghost ak.applet.managed_actor.provision inside the closed four-Event Ghost unit: provision, applet_managed_control PCR genesis, accountability grant and profile create. The conditional Event admission and operation validator require the exact active registration/grant/scope and atomic set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.

Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.member_id == envelope.actor_id using the complete ActorId and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.member_id != envelope.actor_id using the complete ActorId.

Subject-only self-service acceptance. The only authority is that the actor is the invitee of the target Invite (the stored invite_directed_invitee for a directed Invite, the claimed subject for a third-party Invite); an invitee is usually not yet a member and holds no grant, so admission never evaluates a capability and the action is excluded from every derived authority set (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3).

Grants only the third-party cancellation branch of ak.invite.cancel (target_state=revoked by an actor that is not the inviter). The invitee declining (target_state=rejected) and the still-joined inviter cancelling its own Invite are authorized by the Invite's accepted binding alone and never evaluate this grant (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3).
Direct Conversation participant self-leave only. It never authorizes leave/ban/remove of the other participant or any join transition.

Accepted-at compensation for a self-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard leave transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it cannot be transferred or used as ordinary membership authority.

Accepted-at compensation for a delegated/admin-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard remove transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it grants no Realm admin capability.

Direct Conversation exact-pair self-rejoin only. It never authorizes a first join, a third participant, or a join authored on behalf of the other participant, and it never authorizes any grant, policy, admin, Strand or binding change.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects realm_alias). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3.

Terminal Realm lifecycle; v1 production admission MUST reject with failed_precondition and zero writes because the independent destructive-confirmation carrier is undefined. It MUST NOT be granted to anyone.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Held either by the current controller of the realm_authority_root typed current result (root authority, not a grant) or by an ordinary revocable co-owner grant. Both derived sets are rule-generated; hand edits are rejected by tools/artifact_pipeline.py check.

Rotates the controller binding of the Realm authority-root typed current result. Authored only by the current controller with successor acceptance; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.
Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.
Holder-private consent is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm; it is never grantable to a Realm co-owner or another principal.
Holder-private consent revocation is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm and must remove caller-observed dots; it is never grantable.

Advances the Realm authority-root delegation generation, which invalidates every grant descending from a realm_root ref of the previous generation. Authored only by the current controller against the frozen pre-state digest; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set. profiles/conformance-profiles.json lists it in the root-owner mask's allowed_root_control_actions alongside ak.realm.owner.transfer.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.
